A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PanSplat and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H. The complete 24-page versions support reliable comparison, including the supplementary visual results.

before.justification: v1 reports original PanSplat evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, component ablations, frame-distance analyses, and GPU memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, with revised numerical results in several main-text and appendix tables.

M1.justification: The Fibonacci Gaussian pyramid, hierarchical cost volume, Gaussian heads, cubemap renderer, deferred backpropagation, deferred blending, and loss functions remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A, B, and F.

E1.justification: Both versions use Matterport3D, Replica, Residential, 360Loc, and self-captured Insta360 data, retaining the same resolution, narrow/wide-baseline, and frame-distance evaluation scenarios. Revised sampling within 360Loc concerns experimental settings rather than new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Synthetic comparisons retain S-NeRF, OmniSyn, IBRNet, NeuRay, PanoGRF, and MVSplat; real-data comparisons retain MVSplat. Newly cited works, including Splatter-360, are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C changes reported 360Loc fine-tuning from inputs spaced two frames apart with all four views as targets to input spacings of 1–4 frames with one intermediate target. It separately specifies two-frame spacing and four-view evaluation. This is a reported protocol revision; whether it reflects rerunning experiments or correcting documentation is unstated.

E4.justification: The component ablations, frame-distance sensitivity analysis, qualitative examples, and memory-scaling analyses are retained. Tables 3 and E.1 have revised scores, but no ablation variants, analysis questions, or controls are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The revisions do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The preferred WS-PSNR metric is systematically revised across Tables 1–3, D.1, and E.1, changing benchmark winners. In Table 1, PanSplat at Matterport3D 2.0 m changes from 21.19 to 20.56, falling below unchanged PanoGRF at 20.96; Residential changes from 31.36 to 30.97, falling from first to third. Table 2 also replaces unblended PanSplat PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS results. Given the revised fine-tuning description, these real-data changes are not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Gaussian lattice and pyramid definitions, training losses, and deferred-blending equation remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient feed-forward 4K panorama synthesis, superior image quality, memory-efficient training, and up to 70-fold faster inference than PanoGRF.

C2.justification: Appendix D replaces the general statement of best performance across most narrow-baseline metrics with a distinction between best performance at 0.5 m and competitive results at 0.2 m. Mechanism explanations and the limitation concerning dynamic scenes remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the reported code status from a future release to available code at the same repository. Appendix C also distinguishes training and evaluation view sampling more explicitly; architecture, hardware, optimizer, and training-budget disclosures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds concurrent Splatter-360 and distinguishes PanSplat through high-resolution real-world support. It also adds single-view feed-forward reconstruction, Fibonacci-grid, and medical-imaging/robotics references. These are limited additions to the existing research positioning rather than a substantial reframing.

P1.justification: There are limited additions and rewrites in the introduction, related work, and Appendices C and D, plus a new funding acknowledgment. The section organization and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 moves between columns on page 8, ranking highlights change in the comparison tables, and text and references reflow. The figure/table inventory, diagrams, qualitative images, and supplementary plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reported code access, separates training and evaluation sampling, updates related work, and qualifies the 0.2 m conclusion. However, widespread score replacements are unexplained and incompletely reconciled with the presentation: Figure F.1 retains its curves despite Table 2 revisions, and Section 4.2 retains broad superiority wording although Table 1 now places PanSplat below PanoGRF on 2.0 m WS-PSNR. These unresolved consistency issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
